audits.title: Data-driven quality improvement in the Emergency Department at a level one trauma and tertiary care hospital.
audits.standard: CQI metrics: turnaround time, left AMA or without being seen, complaints
audits.setting: Emergency Department, LDS Hospital, Salt Lake City (level one trauma centre)

cycle1.result: Mean quarterly turnaround 183 min; complaints 2.1 per 1000; AMA/LWOBS 2.7%.

audits.intervention: CQI programme with monthly data analysis, data-driven process change and staff education.
audits.other_findings: Volume rose 32% to nearly 37,000 visits/year; 44.8% rated care excellent.
audits.citation: Welch SJ, Allen TL. Data-driven quality improvement in the Emergency Department at a level one trauma and tertiary care hospital. J Emerg Med. 2006;30(3):269-276. doi:10.1016/j.jemermed.2005.07.007. PMID: 16677976.

audits.title: Quality improvement program in an emergency department.
audits.standard: ED quality indicators (length of stay, left against medical advice, left without being seen, 48-hour returns, complaints)
audits.setting: Emergency department, King Abdul-Aziz Hospital, Al-Ahsa

cycle1.result: Unscheduled returns 2%; left against advice 1.5%; left without being seen 1.6%; complaints 1.3 per 1000 patients.

audits.intervention: Monthly data collection and analysis, data-driven process change and staff education in quality concepts

cycle2.result: Unscheduled returns 1%; left against advice 1.2%; left without being seen 0.8%; complaints 0.25 per 1000 patients.

audits.other_findings: Mean monthly length of stay remained static despite a 47% rise in volume to 51,698 visits/year.
audits.citation: Rehmani R, Amatullah AF. Quality improvement program in an emergency department. Saudi Med J. 2008;29(3):418-422. PMID: 18327371.

audits.title: Clinical audit of emergency unit before and after establishment of the emergency medicine department.
audits.standard: Ward-based international standards checklist (staffing, education/CPD, facility, equipment, records, disaster planning and other domains)
audits.setting: Emergency units of six general hospitals affiliated to Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran

cycle1.result: Deficiencies found across domains before establishment of emergency medicine departments (figures not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Education and CPD (p = 0.042), design and facility (p = 0.027), equipment (p = 0.028) and disaster planning (p = 0.026) significantly improved; nearly all domains showed a positive change.

audits.other_findings: Equipment, records, ancillary services, administration and bench-marking showed the lowest improvement.
audits.citation: Amini A, Dindoost P, Moghimi M, Kariman H, Shahrami A, Dolatabadi AA, et al.. Clinical audit of emergency unit before and after establishment of the emergency medicine department. J Pak Med Assoc. 2012;62(2):154-158. PMID: 22755378.

audits.title: An Audit of Emergency Department Accreditation Based on Joint Commission International Standards (JCI).
audits.standard: Iranian hospital accreditation checklist based on JCI standards (24 headings, 337 subheadings)
audits.setting: Emergency department, Shohadaye Tajrish Hospital, Tehran

cycle1.result: Mean total accreditation score 60.4±30.15%; six headings scored below 50%.

audits.intervention: Causes of weak spots identified and corrected.

cycle2.result: Mean total score 68.9±22.9% (p=0.005); data collection and analysis rose 40% and staff competency testing 17% to above 50%.

audits.other_findings: Quality improvement, patient admission and assessment, patient training and facilities stayed below 50%.
audits.citation: Hashemi B, Motamedi M, Etemad M, Rahmati F, Forouzanfar MM, Kaghazchi F. An Audit of Emergency Department Accreditation Based on Joint Commission International Standards (JCI). Emerg (Tehran). 2014;2(3):130-133. PMID: 26495364.

audits.title: Auditing the quality of care in emergency departments.
audits.standard: Physician panel criteria for management of six chief complaints (provisional standards)

cycle1.result: Cases not meeting standards: chest pain 51% (36), abdominal pain 35% (35), wounds 51% (51), sore throat 43% (22).

cycle2.result: Being tabulated; preliminary findings indicate an improvement in cases meeting criteria.

audits.other_findings: Non-physician auditors reviewed records against criteria, with implicit physician review of variances.
audits.citation: Cole L, Cayten CG, Staroscik R. Auditing the quality of care in emergency departments. JACEP. 1976;5(1):32-35. doi:10.1016/s0361-1124(76)80164-5. PMID: 778455.

audits.title: The time relationship of performance and audit feedback on conformance with emergency department process criteria.

cycle1.result: Group with neither audit feedback nor supervision had about half the conformance of the best group.

audits.intervention: Varying time delays in audit feedback and degrees of supervision.

cycle2.result: With daily audit and supervisory feedback, conformance reached 80%, a 100% improvement.

audits.citation: Ognibene M, McNitt H, Wolcott BW. The time relationship of performance and audit feedback on conformance with emergency department process criteria. Ann Emerg Med. 1980;9(3):123-125. doi:10.1016/s0196-0644(80)80265-4. PMID: 6102443.

audits.title: Emergency department chart auditing in a family practice residency program.
audits.setting: Family Practice Residency Program emergency department, Gainesville, Florida

cycle1.result: Care conformed to standards in 85.6%; resident errors in 14.4%, more in early training years (P < .005); management changed in 1%.

audits.other_findings: Inadequate documentation was common at all training levels.
audits.citation: Grauer K. Emergency department chart auditing in a family practice residency program. J Fam Pract. 1983;16(1):121-126. PMID: 6848625.
